agent.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
agent.description: Terminal-native AI coding assistant with agentic capabilities for building, editing, debugging, and understanding code through natural language

avatar.tagline: A master developer's companion that speaks code fluently, wields dozens of tools with precision, yet always defers to human judgment on critical decisions

visualTraits.form: Abstract geometric — 12-sided badge representing Level 0 capability dimensions
visualTraits.symbol: Terminal cursor within a radar chart silhouette

strengths: Repairs plans when builds or tests fail
weaknesses: No memory across sessions without external stores
Cannot learn or improve from past interactions
Purely digital — no physical world interaction
Requires human approval for irreversible actions

capabilityProfile._positionNote: Positions are fixed (0..11). Cognitive Core (0-3) → Action & Integration (4-6) → Trust & Deployment (7-11)

autonomy.evidence: Can decompose complex goals into sub-tasks, delegate to sub-agents, schedule multi-step work, but respects human approval gates for file modifications and tool execution

reasoning.evidence: Plans multi-step implementations, compares approaches, handles branching logic, repairs plans when builds/tests fail. Can orchestrate parallel sub-agents for complex investigations

memory.evidence: Session-level memory with context compaction. Cross-session store for history retrieval. Custom instructions persist. No long-term preference learning across sessions

learning.evidence: Adapts within session via context and conversation history. Incorporates custom instructions and skills. No cross-session learning or model fine-tuning from user feedback

toolUse.evidence: Orchestrates 30+ tools (grep, glob, view, edit, shell, git, GitHub MCP, SQL, web search/fetch, sub-agents). Handles failures, retries, parallel execution, and tool chaining

collaboration.evidence: Delegates to specialized sub-agents (explore, task, research, code-review). Coordinates with GitHub (PRs, issues). Human-in-the-loop approval model. No multi-user agent coordination

embodiment.evidence: Purely digital agent operating within a terminal environment. No physical sensors, actuators, or spatial awareness

explainability.evidence: Explains approach before implementing, provides rationale for tool choices, shows reasoning in responses, summarizes what was done and why. Intent reporting system makes current goals visible

safety.evidence: Content exclusion policies, prohibited actions list, path traversal prevention, secret detection. No formal adversarial testing or circuit-breaker mechanisms

interoperability.evidence: MCP protocol support (client), GitHub API integration, multiple output formats (JSON, Markdown), cross-CLI skill registration. A2A-compatible agent card format

costEfficiency.evidence: No explicit cost tracking or budget awareness. Uses parallel tool calls for efficiency. No model routing based on task complexity. Token usage not exposed to user

domainAlignment.evidence: Permission system with explicit approval gates. Content exclusion policies. Trusted folder model. Audit trail via session history. Respects organizational policies. No formal certification
